text:
zoe: Hi finance, quick question  booked a last-minute intercity bus in Spain, corp card was charged €18.90 but my bank converted and shows $20.15 on my personal account. I paid the difference on my personal card accidentally (small tip). How should I submit for reimbursement? cc @finance
finance-ops: thanks Zoe. Two options: (A) submit the corp charge as-is in Expensify (EUR) and we will reconcile the bank FX when settling; (B) if you want reimbursement for the tip/diff you should submit a separate personal expense with a screenshot showing the $ charge plus the vendor receipt.
zoe: vendor only provided one small printed slip (amount €18.90) and my personal bank screenshot shows $20.15 with a small $1.25 tip on a separate line. I can upload both. Do I need manager approval for the tip?
jen: approving the $1.25 tip as business-appropriate. No extra approval needed. Please tag the personal expense "TIP-EXCEPTION" and link the corp expense ID in the notes.
expense-bot: New expense submitted by zoe  corporate charge: 18.90 EUR (attached: vendor-slip.jpg), personal tip reimbursement: 1.25 USD (attached: bank-snap.png), tags: TIP-EXCEPTION, status: awaiting processing. EXP-2026-4421.
finance-ops: Received. We'll post the EUR reimbursement to the corp card record and process the $1.25 as a personal reimbursement. For FX: we'll use the corporate settlement rate on the merchant date for the EUR item; personal tip will be reimbursed at the bank-posted USD amount. If audit needs any clarification we'll ping you.
zoe: uploaded both files and added note: "card posted EUR 18.90, bank posted USD 20.15; tip $1.25 personal". Thanks!
jen: thanks all, closing once payment posts.
